ownership_summary: Privately held, not listed, with about 65 shareholders (firm's Shareholder Information page, undated). The employee share plan Arqaam Capital SIPCO Limited is the largest holder and no other holder has 10% or more; about 70% is held by a few key investors and over 60% is GCC owned or controlled. Named 5%+ holders: SIPCO, Wafra International Investment Co (PIFSS Kuwait), Emirates NBD, Al Dhow Holding (Al Sayer Group) and Commercial Bank International. Newer investors, stakes undisclosed: Ethmar International Holding of Abu Dhabi (May 2025) and Bader Nasser Al-Kharafi / BNK Group with National Investments Company (NIC) of Kuwait (7 Jul 2026). Checked 12 Oct 2026; no wind-down or sale of the firm found.

group_structure: Arqaam Capital Limited (Cayman) is the pure holding parent. Arqaam Global Markets Limited (Cayman) holds the regulated financial-services business (DIFC, UAE, KSA, Egypt entities, plus Arqaam Capital Research Offshore s.a.l. in Lebanon); Arqaam Capital Principal Finance Limited (Cayman) holds the Arqaam Investment Partners alternatives business; Arqaam Group Central Support Services Limited (DIFC) provides shared services. Arqaam Wealth and Arqaam Digital are listed as 'new initiatives' with no named legal entity. Ownership percentages in subsidiaries are not disclosed. Financial statements are private (auditor Deloitte & Touche (M.E.), year-end 31 Dec).

footprint: Headquarters at Level 27, Unit 2701, Index Tower, DIFC, Dubai. The overview page says five offices in four countries (UAE, KSA, Egypt, Lebanon) while its location list shows Cayman, DIFC, UAE, KSA, Egypt and Lebanon. A physical office in Kuwait is planned (Jul 2026 release). Homepage counters show 5 regional offices and about 200 staff (S1, S2, S16). Checked 2026-10-12.
customer_segments: Institutional investors (sales and trading, research, corporate access), corporates and governments (investment banking), and high-net-worth individuals and family offices (Arqaam Wealth and the equities business). No retail or mass-affluent proposition found.
business_lines: Four business lines on the website: Arqaam Markets (sales and trading, brokerage, market making, derivatives, credit trading, research, investment banking, asset management, wealth), Arqaam Principal (Arqaam Investment Partners alternatives), Arqaam Wealth and Arqaam Digital (new initiatives; Digital has no public description). Asset management runs Fixed Income (FIAM) and Equities (EQAM) strategies with three open-ended funds and discretionary mandates. Research covers over 230 stocks with 26 analysts. Investment banking covers M&A, ECM and DCM. (Sources: S9-S14.)

capabilities.wealth_summary: Arqaam is an independent, DIFC-headquartered investment bank, broker and asset manager (est. 2007) whose clients are mainly institutions, with a smaller wealth offer. Arqaam Wealth is described as independent global wealth management for high-net-worth and family-office clients, on discretionary and non-discretionary bases, with portfolio construction, advisory, outsourced CIO, custodian-risk diversification and consolidated reporting; no minimum, platform or head is published. Asset management runs three open-ended funds (MENA Bond Income, Islamic Income, Capital Value) and discretionary mandates; the firm reported USD 1.7bn of AUM across wealth and asset management in May 2025 (press report of a company figure). The DFSA Category 2 licence covers dealing, advising, managing assets and collective funds, with an Islamic Window, and the markets arm offers brokerage (GCC and Egypt, access to 40 exchanges), market making, derivatives and structured products. Arqaam Digital is named as a new initiative but has no public description. Fresh capital came from Ethmar (May 2025) and BNK Group with NIC (Jul 2026).

No named head, minimum or client-asset figure published.

asset_management.detail: Fixed Income (FIAM: global bonds and sukuk, conventional and Shariah universe) and Equities (EQAM: listed MENA equities) teams run three open-ended funds (Arqaam MENA Bond Income Fund, Arqaam Islamic Income Fund, Arqaam Capital Value Fund) plus discretionary mandates. USD 1.7bn AUM across wealth and asset management (May 2025, press report). Sukuk Fund of the Year at the Global Banking & Markets Awards (Jun 2026) and Lipper recognition for the Islamic Income Fund (Jun 2026). Fund domiciles and sizes not stated.

brokerage.detail: Arqaam Securities LLC (UAE CMA brokerage, IPO and market-making licences) and Arqaam Securities Brokerage S.A.E. (Egypt: equities brokerage, margin trading, intraday, GDR). Offers direct market access and a unified algo suite through in-house ArqNeT, access to 40 exchanges globally, and market making on DFM, ADX and Tadawul. Homepage shows USD 43.7bn trading volume in 2025 (company counter). Institutional focus with HNW and family-office clients served by the equities business.

digital_investing.detail: Arqaam Digital is listed as a business line and as a 'new initiative' with no named entity, product or launch date; its page returned 404. The only digital channel found is institutional (ArqNeT electronic execution). No retail app found.

advisory.detail: Investment advisory is a stated wealth service, and the DFSA licence covers advising on financial products and on credit; Saudi CMA advising licence for Arqaam Capital Financial Company.

discretionary.detail: Wealth management 'on a discretionary and non-discretionary basis' and discretionary mandates in both fixed-income and equity strategies; DFSA 'managing assets' permission; Saudi CMA managing-investments licence (resolution 13 May 2025).

model_portfolios_robo.detail: The Research page cites a 'MENA Equity Core' model portfolio (27.9% a year since May 2012, past performance) that can be shared with clients via Bloomberg. It is a research product, not a client robo or model-portfolio service.

funds_platform.detail: Only Arqaam's own three mutual funds were found. The wealth page lists funds among products within 'the full range of Arqaam products and services' but names no third-party fund shelf or platform provider.

structured_products.detail: Derivatives desk covers options, futures, swaps and structured products, OTC and exchange-traded; the DFSA licence scope lists structured products. Distribution to wealth clients not described.

private_markets.detail: Arqaam Principal / Arqaam Investment Partners holds alternative investments: a luxury hotel and residences project in Hvar (Croatia), gold mining in Mongolia expanding into Kazakhstan, Agripower (Australia), Wego (Singapore) and Quiqup (UK). The wealth page lists 'alternatives' in the product range; whether these are offered to wealth clients is not stated.

islamic_wealth.detail: DFSA Islamic Window endorsement; Arqaam Islamic Income Fund (open-ended, Shariah Supervisory Board of Sheikh Dr. Nazih Hammad, Sheikh Dr. Amin Fateh and Sheikh Dr. Muhammad Amin Qattan); sukuk strategies; Sukuk Fund of the Year award (Jun 2026).

discrepancies.detail: The firm's Shareholder Information page (S4, undated) lists SIPCO, Wafra, Emirates NBD, Al Dhow and CBI and does not mention Ethmar (May 2025), BNK/NIC (Jul 2026) or Qatar Insurance Company, which Enterprise AM lists as an existing shareholder (S21).
discrepancies.resolution: Recorded all as shareholders with the source for each; percentages are not disclosed and the official page appears out of date.

discrepancies.detail: The overview page says 'five offices in four countries' but lists six entries (Cayman, DIFC, UAE, KSA, Egypt, Lebanon); the homepage counter shows 5 regional offices.
discrepancies.resolution: Treated as five operating offices plus the Cayman holding entity.

discrepancies.field: Company status (lead from task notes: wind-down or acquisition)
discrepancies.detail: No wind-down, sale or merger of Arqaam found. The firm is operating and issuing releases to 29 Sep 2026, and took new investment in May 2025 and Jul 2026. A Bloomberg report of May 2019 on merger talks with The National Investor is the only merger item and no completed deal was found.
discrepancies.resolution: Recorded as an active private investment bank; the lead is not supported.

discrepancies.detail: The firm's overview (S2) and Bloomberg via Gulf News (2019, S24) say 2007; The National (12 Dec 2012) says Arqaam 'was set up in early 2008' and launched with four staff (S39). Aggregator profiles (not cited) give other start years for individual group entities.
discrepancies.resolution: Used 2007 (the firm's own statement) for the CEO's appointed year and noted 2008 in appointed_note; unresolved.

discrepancies.detail: Firm sources use different titles for the same person: 'Managing Director for Fixed Income Asset Management' (31 Dec 2024, S34), 'Head of Fixed Income' (1 Dec 2025, S33), 'CIO' of the Arqaam Islamic Income Fund (Aug 2026 factsheet, S36); Gulf News 2018 'head of Fixed Income Asset Management' (S29).
discrepancies.resolution: Treated as one role (head of the fixed-income asset-management business); all titles recorded in the person's title and appointed_note.

open_items: DFSA public register pages returned 403, so the licence category and permitted activities for Arqaam Capital Limited (F000407 per search results) were taken from the firm's own Regulatory Status page (S3). Check the DFSA register, the UAE CMA and Saudi CMA registers directly.
No licence numbers or dates are published on the firm's site. The UAE CMA and Egyptian FRA permits are company statements only.

Financial statements are private (S6): total assets, income and profit are not available. AUM of USD 1.7bn (May 2025) is a press-reported company figure; the Jul 2026 Forbes post says AUM has grown but gives no number.
Arqaam Digital: page returned 404; scope unknown. Check whether it includes any wealth or investing app.
Homepage statistics (staff 200, trading volume USD 43.7bn in 2025, 230 research stocks) were read from script-rendered counter markup; confirm visually in a browser. 'B / $' was read as USD billion.
The Saudi CMA managing-investments licence is from an Argaam report whose date is ambiguous (02/10/2025); the CMA announcement itself (CMA_N_3886, seen in search results) was not opened.
Fund domiciles, sizes and fund managers for the three mutual funds are not stated; older Arqaam funds (value fund, macro hedge fund) appear in search results only and their current status is unknown.
The task notes suggested a possible acquisition or wind-down; none was found (see discrepancies).
Governance pages (S7, S8) name no directors or executives; the firm's investment banking page (S14) lists services but no transactions or people.

Board and governance: the Board of Directors page linked from the Governance page returns 404 and the Advisory Board is 'Coming soon' (S8); archive.org lists a 12 Jul 2024 snapshot of /board-of-directors/ but web.archive.org cannot be reached from this environment. Only the Chairman (Sami Sindi) is named; other directors and the General Counsel, COO, Arqaam Global Markets president and Arqaam Investment Partners MD (roles on the Advisory Members page, S48) are not named in any source found. Sindi's career and education are not published in an opened source.

Added in this pass: Sami Sindi (Chairman; the file had no chair) and Hani Shalabi (head of equities execution / brokerage). Named on official posts but not profiled: Hazem Abdel-Mohsen (UAE Country Head, post of 15 Feb 2026), Mehdi Popotte (portfolio manager, Islamic Income Fund, S36), Nadim Amatouri (Director of credit research), Danya Bashir (Director of Special Projects), and unnamed heads of debt solutions & DCM and of ECM execution (posts of Jun and Aug 2025).

No head of Arqaam Wealth, of equities asset management (EQAM) or of Arqaam Digital is named on the official site or in the posts read (the Nov 2023 board post mentions the launch of the Wealth Management division, S30).

Riad Meliti: education is not published in an opened source (The National says only 'educated on the US west coast'; not recorded); DFSA register page returned 403 (S25). A search summary mentioned a LinkedIn post by an Arqaam employee referring to 'our CEO, Mohamed Hesham' at an Abu Dhabi Investment Forum event in London; not opened, unverified (may concern a unit or another firm); all 2025-2026 firm sources name Riad Meliti as CEO.
Karim Baghdady: HR Today (March 2026) returned 403 and the ABANA page is undated; no Arqaam post announces him. Re-check Arqaam's own news or a management page.

LinkedIn (2026-10-13): official links recorded for Abdul Kadir Hussain and Paolo Casamassima (from Arqaam posts); search-result matches for Jaap Meijer and Hani Shalabi; no profile found for the CEO, the Chairman or Karim Baghdady (role-based searches only). The Shari'ah scholars were not checked.
Shari'ah Supervisory Board: biographies come from the 20 Jul 2023 prospectus (S37, hosted by Ajman Bank); no later change was searched. The Aug 2026 factsheet (S36) does not list members.
